title: ICAB C7 - Information Technology
summary: Covers systems analysis and design (SDLC), agile development, cloud computing, enterprise software (ERP), database management, business intelligence, and cybersecurity.

all.name: Full Syllabus Tracker
all.blurb: Official 2025 Syllabus chapter and topic tracker for Information Technology. Track your study progress across all syllabus areas.

stages.title: Area 1: Building Information Systems & SDLC
stages.name: Area 1: Building Information Systems & SDLC
stages.description: System development lifecycle, project governance, feasibility analysis, agile vs waterfall.

nodes.name: SDLC, Feasibility Analysis & Agile Methodologies
nodes.description: Building information systems; project governance and management; business case and feasibility analysis (TELOS: Technical, Economic, Legal, Operational, Schedule); System Development Lifecycle (SDLC) stages: Planning, Analysis, Design, Implementation, Testing, Maintenance; Waterfall vs Agile/Scrum methodologies; system changeover strategies (Direct, Parallel, Pilot, Phased).
topics: System development need identification and business case formulation
Feasibility study: Technical, Economic, Legal, Operational, Schedule (TELOS)
SDLC phases: Requirements engineering, architectural design, coding, testing
Waterfall model vs Agile / Scrum methodology (sprints, standups, user stories)
Software testing methods: Unit, integration, system, user acceptance testing (UAT)
System changeover strategies: Direct cutover, parallel run, pilot, phased adoption
Post-implementation review and ongoing system maintenance
learningOutcomes: Conduct a TELOS feasibility study for an enterprise software acquisition.
Compare Waterfall and Agile methodologies for business applications.
checklists: Review comparison table between 4 system changeover methods
Practice TELOS feasibility analysis on a real business scenario
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 2: Cloud Computing & Enterprise Systems
stages.name: Area 2: Cloud Computing & Enterprise Systems
stages.description: Cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), ERP architectures, supply chain systems.

nodes.name: Cloud Architectures & Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)
nodes.description: Cloud service delivery models: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), Software as a Service (SaaS); cloud deployment models (Public, Private, Hybrid); Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems (SAP, Oracle, Odoo); Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Supply Chain Management (SCM) systems.
topics: Cloud computing concepts, elasticity, multi-tenancy, pay-per-use economics
Service models: SaaS (QuickBooks Online, Salesforce), PaaS (AWS Elastic Beanstalk), IaaS (Azure VMs)
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) architecture, centralized database, module integration
ERP implementation challenges: Change management, data migration, customization risks
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Supply Chain Management (SCM) integration
Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and cloud vendor risk governance
learningOutcomes: Differentiate SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS models and select appropriate solutions.
Explain the architecture and strategic benefits of integrated ERP systems.
Assess operational risks associated with cloud service adoption.
checklists: Map enterprise business processes into standard ERP modules
Evaluate cloud SLA key performance metrics
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 3: Data Management, BI & AI Foundations
stages.name: Area 3: Data Management, BI & AI Foundations
stages.description: Relational databases, SQL concepts, data warehousing, BI analytics, AI/ML in accounting.

nodes.name: DBMS, SQL, Business Intelligence & Applied AI
nodes.description: Database Management Systems (DBMS); relational data models, primary keys, foreign keys, normalization; basic SQL queries (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY); Data Warehousing and ETL pipelines; Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards; Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning applications in accounting and auditing.
topics: Relational database concepts: Entities, attributes, tables, relationships (1:1, 1:N, M:N)
Database normalization concepts (1NF, 2NF, 3NF) for transactional integrity
SQL fundamentals for financial audit data extraction
Data warehouses vs Data lakes vs Operational transactional databases
Business Intelligence (BI) tools: Data visualization and executive reporting
Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Natural Language Processing (NLP)
Automating financial reconciliation and anomaly detection using algorithmic models
learningOutcomes: Explain relational database structure and normalization principles.
Describe how data warehouses and ETL support business analytics.
Identify practical applications of AI and machine learning in finance.
checklists: Practice basic SQL SELECT and JOIN statements
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 4: Information Security & Cyber Resilience
stages.name: Area 4: Information Security & Cyber Resilience
stages.description: Cybersecurity threats, CIA triad, access controls, disaster recovery, data protection laws.

nodes.name: CIA Triad, Cyber Controls & Disaster Recovery
nodes.description: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA triad); common cyber threats: Malware, Phishing, Ransomware, DDoS, Social Engineering; technical and physical controls: Firewalls, encryption, multi-factor authentication (MFA); Business Continuity Planning (BCP) and Disaster Recovery Planning (DRP); Bangladesh Cyber Security Act 2023.
topics: The CIA triad: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability principles
Cyber threat taxonomy: Phishing, Spear-phishing, Ransomware, Man-in-the-middle, Zero-day
Access controls: Role-based access control (RBAC), Least privilege, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
Data encryption: In-transit (TLS/SSL) and at-rest (AES-256)
Backup strategies: Full, differential, incremental; 3-2-1 backup rule
Business Continuity Planning (BCP) and Disaster Recovery Planning (DRP): RTO and RPO metrics
Legal framework: Cyber Security Act 2023 obligations and data protection
learningOutcomes: Apply the CIA triad to assess enterprise information risks.
Formulate disaster recovery strategies incorporating RTO and RPO targets.
checklists: Master RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective) definitions
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)
